<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

MEASURED 2026-09-02: `flowspace3 get conv:<guid>#t1` succeeds only when the conversation's anchor worktree equals the cwd's. From the flowspace3 main checkout, conv:8c285d65 (same repo, anchored to a since-tidied worktree) returns FS3-E-QUERY-NOT-FOUND with the message 'no conversation 8c285d65… is indexed' — false; `conversation list` shows it one command earlier; `--repo all` returns ok:true. Every pij and dd conversation behaves the same. `get`'s own help promises the opposite: 'from the INDEX, so it answers for every registered repository, not only the one you are standing in.' This is the verdict-cannot-lie family: a probe that cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'outside my scope' reports data loss. It nearly cost harness-engineering 250 wasted backfill dispatches — their planned --verify would have read 'never delivered' for conversations sitting in the index. They are now holding --verify entirely until this plan ships a verb that cannot be held wrong. The guid is derived, not minted (crates/daemon/src/convo_ingest.rs:341 — sha256 of fs3-convo-v1:{harness}/{session_id}, first 32 hex laid out 8-4-4-4-12 with FORCED version nibble 8 and variant nibble a; positions 12 and 16 of the digest are DROPPED). Every client that reimplements that layout can drift from it silently; the verb exists so none has to. Daemon-side message around crates/daemon/src/conversations.rs:274-358; HTTP in crates/daemon/src/http.rs:304-346. Ruling context: backlog row 101 asked whether an explicit conv: address should be address-authoritative — this measurement is the evidence; o-prime rules YES, subject to Jordan.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- An explicit conv:<guid> address is address-authoritative: `get` resolves it index-wide regardless of cwd, with no flag.
- No not-found on a conv address ever claims global absence for a scope decision: the two cases carry two messages and two `details` shapes.
- `flowspace3 conversation verify --harness <h> --session <id>` (and `--pij <seat>` via the existing join) answers delivered-or-not under the consumer's contract: exit 0 + ok:true with guid/address/turns/repo/worktree/last-turn ⇒ delivered; a DISTINCT not-indexed code ⇒ not; repo-unscoped by construction — no flag can narrow it.
- Docs and help text describe the shipped behaviour, so `get --help`'s promise is true again.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- No change to el: address resolution (they carry their repo).
- No identity union across pij generations (row 121 — waits on pij req-0033); `verify --pij` on an rs seat fails with a message that SAYS the join is legacy-only, nothing more.
- No change to the embed path, ingest cursors, or ranking.
- No `--verify` on the harness side — that is the consumer's, built after this ships.
